title: A kept take is 'proven' on one scored dimension of three
body:
## Summary
rubric.ts isProven reads the mean alone, so a kept music take with only melody scored 9 is proven while 2 of 3 dimensions are absent.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/audio/rubric.ts:64-69 `isProven` = kept && rubricMean >= 7; rubricMean averages the dimensions present (rubric.ts:57-62). readRubric reports `scored`/`of` beside the mean but the verdict ignores it. scoring-rubrics (software-engineering, registry-map state `deviation` at rubric.ts:68) asks a composite verdict to require its coverage. The same rule lives in lib/sound (v1 readVerdict, the ledger's score), pinned equal by tests/next-server/decision-v1-audio-insight.test.ts:129-134, so the fix spans this context and lib/sound (out of scope here).

## Flow
- rate a kept take melody 9 only -> readRubric: scored 1 of 3, proven true -> RubricCard draws the 'proven' chip
- fix: isProven also requires scored === of (or a stated minimum coverage), in rubric.ts AND lib/sound's verdict, with the parity test extended

## Expected impact
The operator stops seeing 'proven' on a take judged on one axis; the Library/knowledge proven counts may fall. Could break: any stored count of proven takes moves.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - proven means the rubric was actually applied
Before: 1-of-3-scored kept take at 9 is proven (walked from rubric.ts:64-69)
After: not proven until coverage is met
Method: simulation - the rule is in two implementations, one out of this context's paths; a worker owning both can gate it
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: a case in packages/ui/test/components/insight.test.ts (kept, 1 of 3 scored at 9 -> not proven) plus the same bag in decision-v1-audio-insight.test.ts's parity loop over lib/sound's verdict; red on main, green on the arm
drain_note: coverage minimum is a product call; L

title: A one-shot effect's card can show a mean over a dimension its breakdown hides
body:
## Summary
readRubric's dims drop loop_seam for a one-shot effect, but its mean is rubricMean over RUBRIC.sfx, which still reads a stored loop_seam; a legacy bag then shows a mean the visible dimensions do not average to.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/audio/rubric.ts:83-90: `dims` = dimsFor(t) (no loop_seam when loop !== true) while `mean` = rubricMean(kind, ratings) over RUBRIC[kind] (rubric.ts:57-62), the ledger's score by design (pinned to lib/sound). checkRatings refuses loop_seam on a one-shot today (rubric.ts:113-114), so only bags written before that door, or a take whose loop flag changed, carry it. Whether any exist is a store question.

## Flow
- sfx take, loop false, ratings {event_match 8, sound_quality 8, loop_seam 2} -> card draws 8, 8, 'scored 2 of 2', mean 6.0, not proven

## Expected impact
If such bags exist the card contradicts itself; if none exist the finding closes. Could break: aligning the mean changes the ledger's score parity.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the mean averages what the card shows
Before: unknown count of affected bags
After: 0
Method: simulation - counting needs the operator's store (foundry-out/gravitone.sqlite, never opened by a session)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
instrument: operator-only: count sfx takes with loop !== true whose ratings carry loop_seam, on the operator's store

title: lib/sound/knowledge.ts keeps a third literal evidence floor
body:
## Summary
The strengths floor is now one constant in @gt/ui (strengths.ts MIN_N, read by lesson.ts), but lib/sound/knowledge.ts:30 declares its own MIN_N = 3 for the knowledge file's claims.

## Description
lib/sound/knowledge.ts:15 says 'The floor is MIN_N, stated in both files' - two literals by admission. lib/sound already imports @gt/ui audio modules (lib/sound/lessons.ts uses lesson.ts cellLesson), so it can read strengths.ts MIN_N. Out of this context's paths.

## Flow
- fix: lib/sound/knowledge.ts imports MIN_N from @gt/ui/components/audio/strengths.ts and drops its literal and the 'stated in both files' sentence

## Expected impact
Raising the table's floor then raises the knowledge file's. Could break: an import cycle if strengths.ts ever imports lib/sound (it does not).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one floor
Before: 2 literal floors (strengths.ts:50, knowledge.ts:30)
After: 1
Method: probe - git grep on both files; not built because the site is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: git grep -nE "MIN_N = [0-9]" -- lib packages: 2 -> 1, plus the knowledge test green

title: The rubric's score steps are 12px-tall touch targets
body:
## Summary
RubricCard draws ten score steps per dimension at height var(--sp-5) (12px) with 1px gaps; on a phone each step is about 16x12px.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/audio/Rubric.module.css:228 `.step{height:var(--sp-5)}`; .steps is a 10-column grid with var(--sp-hair) gaps (:227); .dim gives the steps 1fr after a 52px label and a 36px score (:223). WCAG 2.5.8 asks 24x24 CSS px (or spacing that clears a 24px circle). The number row is the keyboard path; touch has only these steps.

## Flow
- open /audio rubric at 390px -> a dimension row -> each step ~16x12px
- fix: step height to a 24px token on coarse pointers (@media (pointer: coarse)), leaving the desktop meter as drawn

## Expected impact
A phone judge can score without mis-taps. Could break: the card grows taller on touch; the desktop look is unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a score step is tappable
Before: 12px tall (computed from tokens; not photographed)
After: 24px on coarse pointers
Method: simulation - no dev server or capture allowed in this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: pipeline/cx-capture.mjs on the audio rubric screen at --width 390 under a coarse-pointer emulation, step boxes measured from the DOM before/after

title: A strength cell's aria-label names a defect its face hides
body:
## Summary
Cell's aria-label adds 'most often <defect>' whenever topDefect is set, while the face and StrengthHead draw it only when rejected > 0.

## Description
packages/ui/src/components/audio/Strengths.tsx Cell (aria-label vs the `cell.rejected > 0` guard). lib/sound/insights.ts:88-102 counts defects only from rejected takes, so topDefect !== null implies rejected > 0 on every real cell.

## Flow
- walked: no ledger can produce topDefect with rejected 0

## Expected impact
None in practice.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the two channels agree
Before: 0 reachable divergent cells
After: 0
Method: probe - read the producer of topDefect
Result: not-better
Gate: none
